title: There is, there was, etc.
subtitle: There was a loud bang / There being no evidence ...
summary: Introduce new people and things with there + be, make the verb agree with what follows, and use there being in formal writing.

lesson.heading: Introducing something new
lesson.text: To say that a person or thing exists, happens or is found somewhere, we start the sentence with **there + be**. In questions we invert the pattern.

examples.text: **There was** a loud bang from upstairs.
examples.wrong: A loud bang was from upstairs

examples.text: **There's** nothing to eat.
**Is there** anybody in here?

lesson.heading: Other verbs after there
lesson.text: **there** also works with auxiliary and modal verbs, with verb + *to be*, and with a few other verbs that indicate existence.

examples.text: **There must be** some way of contacting her.
**There appears to be** a major disagreement between the two presidents.
examples.note: also used to be, is supposed to be, tends to be, seems to be

examples.text: During the 1990s **there arose** a demand for organic food.

lesson.heading: Indefinite nouns follow there + be
lesson.text: Because there + be introduces a topic, the noun after it usually has an indefinite or non-specific meaning: *a / an*, no article, *any(one)*, *some(thing)*, *no(body)*. A definite noun phrase - the, this, my, your, or a name - is normally the subject of an ordinary sentence instead.

examples.text: **There's** nobody here. / **There was** something strange about her.
The cat was in the kitchen.
examples.note: more usual than There was the cat in the kitchen; but compare There was a cat in the kitchen.

examples.text: Jan is waiting for me outside.
examples.note: more usual than There is Jan waiting for me outside.

lesson.note: There + be + the does occur when we change the topic: ... And then there is the question of who is going to pay.

lesson.heading: Singular or plural?
lesson.text: The verb should agree with the noun that comes after it. If the noun phrase is a list, the first noun decides.

examples.text: **There is** a very good reason for my decision.
**There were** too many people trying to get into the football stadium.
When I opened the fridge **there was** only a bottle of milk, some eggs, and butter.
When I opened the fridge **there were** only some eggs, a bottle of milk, and butter.

lesson.note: In informal speech we sometimes hear there's before a plural noun: 'Well, there's some apples on the table.'

lesson.heading: there + be + noun + clause
lesson.text: A noun after there + be is often followed by a that-, wh-, to-infinitive or -ing clause.

examples.text: Is **there a chance (that)** Kim could arrive this afternoon?
**There is no reason (why)** I can't see you tomorrow.
**There is a small stream which / that runs** at the bottom of the garden.
**There was an attempt to resolve** the dispute at the factory.
**There was a taxi waiting** outside the hotel.

lesson.note: Keep the relative pronoun when it is the subject of the following verb; you can leave it out when it is the object.

lesson.heading: there being
lesson.text: In formal English a clause with **there being** introduces a reason for something.

examples.text: **There being** no evidence against him, he was released.
examples.note: = Because there was no evidence against him

examples.text: **There being** no reports of adverse reactions, the drug is to be sold more widely.

lesson.text: Before choosing there + be, check the noun: if it is your, the, my or a name, an ordinary sentence is almost always better.

exercises.prompt: There ___ no direct rail link between the cities.
exercises.explanation: link is singular, so the verb is singular.

exercises.prompt: There ___ two pubs and a church on the village green.
exercises.explanation: The first noun in the list, two pubs, is plural, so the verb is plural.

exercises.statement: There is your dinner in the oven.
exercises.explanation: Your dinner is in the oven. Your dinner is definite, so there + be is unlikely.

exercises.prompt: There ___ a shower, television, and two single beds in each room.
exercises.explanation: The first noun in the list, a shower, is singular, so the verb is singular.
In questions the subject and verb are inverted: Is there ... ?

exercises.statement: There used to be an art gallery around here.
exercises.explanation: Correct. there works with verb + to be patterns such as used to be, seems to be and is supposed to be.

exercises.prompt: Would a sentence beginning There ... work here?

items.text: Your dinner is in the oven.
No petrol was available anywhere in the city.
The doctor is free to see you now.
An art gallery used to be around here.

exercises.prompt: There ___ no easy answers to the problem of climate change.
exercises.explanation: answers is plural, so we need are - this sentence comes from written English, where there's before a plural is avoided.

exercises.prompt: Join the halves. Add a relative pronoun in your head where one is needed.

pairs.left: There were a lot of people at the party
There's a cake in the kitchen
pairs.right: I've made especially for your birthday.
that Bruno would get the job.
that an election will be held next month.

pairs.left: There aren't many people alive today
There are still some old houses in the village

exercises.statement: There is a small stream runs at the bottom of the garden.
exercises.explanation: There is a small stream which / that runs at the bottom of the garden. We don't leave out a relative pronoun that is the subject of the following verb.

exercises.prompt: Rewrite 'There was no further business, so the meeting closed at 12:30' in formal style, beginning There being ... .
exercises.answer: There being no further business, the meeting closed at 12:30.
exercises.explanation: There being + noun phrase gives the reason for what follows.

exercises.prompt: Rewrite 'Because the facilities were inadequate at the hotel, the conference was relocated' beginning There being ... .
exercises.answer: There being inadequate facilities at the hotel, the conference was relocated to a nearby university.
exercises.explanation: There being replaces a whole because-clause in formal written English.
